title: test(plugin-auth): bring the five scrypt-bound auth test files under the 10 s budget
body:
Refs #23184 (plugin-auth rows)
Clause-②: no — test wall time only; no published schema, behaviour or export moves.

A partial landing of the `domain:services` test-budget card. This PR answers five of the ten `@objectstack/plugin-auth` rows: the five that share one cause. The other five plugin-auth rows, and the other packages' rows, are not addressed here, and #23184 remains open for them (named below, with what each one waits on).

## Rows this PR answers

| file | card reading (hourly full battery) | before, median of 3 | after, median of 3 | speed-up |
|:--|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| `src/platform-admin-standing.consolidation.test.ts` | 48.7 s | 17.69 s | **1.79 s** | 9.9x |
| `src/admin-impersonate-endpoint.test.ts` | 11.9 s | 11.81 s | **1.62 s** | 7.3x |
| `src/session-grants-resolved-once.test.ts` | 10.8 s | 10.61 s | **2.42 s** | 4.4x |
| `src/two-factor-reenrollment-verified-reset.test.ts` | 14.1 s | 6.59 s | **1.24 s** | 5.3x |
| `src/two-factor-rotated-token-echo.test.ts` | 31.3 s | 9.59 s | **2.20 s** | 4.4x |

Tests only: no production file, option or export changes. Every case and every `expect` line is unchanged (proof below).

## What the five files were waiting on (measured)

- **H1 holds: production-parameter scrypt (N=16384, r=16) dominated.** A temporary probe wrapped `node:crypto.scrypt` and counted derivations per case. At the base, the five files ran 130 / 95 / 86 / 48 / 63 real derivations (consolidation / admin-impersonate / session-grants / re-enrollment / rotated-token), about 0.115 s each on this box: 85 / 84 / 85 / 79 / 73 percent of their case wall. Every sign-up hashes under a fresh salt, and every later sign-in or password check derives the same password against the same salt again.
- **A second shared cost: the re-registered bearer-rotation suite.** All five files import `createMemoryEngine` from `impersonation-bearer-rotation.test.ts`, which re-registers that file's 10 cases in each importer (a trade `admin-impersonate-endpoint.test.ts` documents at its import). Those 10 cases cost 4.4 to 4.9 s of each file's local wall at the base, 20 derivations each time.
- **H2: no per-case kernel boot dominated.** A second probe split the time by entry point: an `AuthManager` instance after the first costs 8 to 21 ms, and a sign-in that the memo answers about 7 ms. What did show up is the vendor's first module load, paid inside the first clocked case: the first instance in a file costs 540 to 800 ms against 8 to 21 ms for later ones, because `AuthManager` reaches better-auth through lazy `await import()` calls.
- **H3: one test-only helper serves all five**, with no production seam: `src/__tests__/scrypt-memo.testkit.ts`.

## What changed

1. **`src/__tests__/scrypt-memo.testkit.ts` (new, test-only).** A per-file memo of `node:crypto.scrypt`, keyed by every input (password, salt, key length, options). scrypt is pure, so a hit answers the bytes a fresh call returns; any input not seen before (every fresh salt) runs the real derivation; a concurrent request for an input in flight waits for it. better-auth is loaded natively by vitest, so `vi.mock('node:crypto')` cannot reach it; the memo is set on the builtin's exports object and published with Node's `syncBuiltinESMExports()`, and `restore()` (in `afterAll`) puts the original back the same way. Installs share one memo per module graph and the original returns with the last restore. No tsup entry reaches the file.
2. **Fixture sign-ups made once per file** in `platform-admin-standing.consolidation.test.ts`, `admin-impersonate-endpoint.test.ts` and `impersonation-bearer-rotation.test.ts` (`signedUpOnce`). The users each case starts from are signed up once through the real `/sign-up/email` route on an engine and manager of their own; each case then starts from a `structuredClone` of those tables on its own engine and its own manager, and every step from the standing seed or grant on runs per case as before (seed, sign-in, gates). No case in these files is about the sign-up itself. Probes below show the cloned start state equals a per-case sign-up's, and that copies are isolated.
3. **Isolated suites run concurrently** (`describe.concurrent`), so the derivations that remain overlap on the libuv pool. Each case builds its own engine and manager. Two suites stay sequential, each for a stated reason:
   - consolidation's fail-closed floor: its first case asserts that a `vi.spyOn` spy saw no call, and another case's `restoreAllMocks` lifting the spy mid-case would let that pass on a dead spy;
   - admin-impersonate's "exactly one plugin claims the path": it reads what `console.error` received while its own manager booted.
   - In `two-factor-rotated-token-echo.test.ts` the SqlDriver engines are now closed in `afterAll` instead of `afterEach` (an `afterEach` would close a database a concurrent case still holds), so that suite runs concurrently too.
   The console stubs every file installs in `beforeEach` are the only other shared state; a sibling's `restoreAllMocks` can lift them early, which costs log output and no assertion (no case in these suites reads them; on the rotated-token file the output was 127 lines after against 126 before).
4. **better-auth's first module load at module top** in the five files: side-effect imports of the vendor modules their managers boot through, following AGENTS.md's rule that clocked windows measure behaviour, never loading (the same thing `session-grants-resolved-once.test.ts` already does for `@objectstack/core`). Nothing a case runs changes: the module cache hands `AuthManager` the same instances, and none of these files changes an environment the vendor reads at load (better-auth captures `NODE_ENV` when its env module is first evaluated).

**About the bearer-rotation file.** `impersonation-bearer-rotation.test.ts` is not one of the ten rows, and it is outside the claim's file list. I changed it because it is what these five files wait on: its 10 cases run inside each of them. It gets the memo, the once-per-file sign-ups and concurrent suites; its own cases and `expect` lines are unchanged. The same import also reaches the 10 other plugin-auth files that import it, so their copies of those cases get faster as well; the whole package is green (below).

## Proof

**Wall time.** The reading is vitest's per-file duration, the JSON reporter's `endTime - startTime` (the figure the module line prints and the hourly captures parse). Each file ran alone, in `packages/plugins/plugin-auth`, under the shared verify lock, three runs each, with the same command:

`pnpm exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 FILE --reporter=verbose --reporter=json --outputFile.json=OUT`

| file | before @ `4f5679c261` (ms) | after @ `7fcbf26fa4` (ms) |
|:--|:--|:--|
| consolidation | 17478 / 18010 / 17693 | 1892 / 1747 / 1791 |
| admin-impersonate | 11811 / 11725 / 12032 | 1513 / 1636 / 1617 |
| session-grants | 11481 / 10397 / 10613 | 2423 / 2574 / 2341 |
| re-enrollment | 6329 / 6593 / 6823 | 1198 / 1449 / 1241 |
| rotated-token | 9661 / 9261 / 9587 | 2219 / 2162 / 2196 |

The box is shared with other agents; the ratios are the robust part.

**CI projection.** From the `test-core-timing-table` artifacts of five recent hourly full-battery runs (`38394406081`, `38387445301`, `38380636705`, `38373927133`, `38366978022`), the worst CI/local ratio per file and the after-median times that ratio:

| file | CI readings (s) | worst ratio | projection | at the card's own ratio |
|:--|:--|--:|--:|--:|
| consolidation | 33.5 / 39.1 / 13.4 / 28.2 / 30.6 | 2.21 | **4.0 s** | 4.9 s (2.75) |
| admin-impersonate | 18.7 / 19.1 / 9.5 / 9.6 / 14.6 | 1.62 | **2.6 s** | 1.6 s (1.01) |
| session-grants | 9.8 / 12.5 / 8.5 / 8.8 / 8.2 | 1.18 | **2.8 s** | 2.5 s (1.02) |
| re-enrollment | 9.5 / 15.9 / 5.3 / 8.8 / 12.7 | 2.41 | **3.0 s** | 2.7 s (2.14) |
| rotated-token | 19.4 / 24.4 / 9.4 / 17.6 / 19.1 | 2.55 | **5.6 s** | 7.2 s (3.26) |

One caveat, stated because it moves the margin: these ratios were measured on the old, sequential shapes. The one concurrent shape with a CI reading so far, the previous slice's `share-link-password.test.ts`, read 4.8 s and 4.2 s (push run `38395837748`, merge group `38393091761`) against 1.18 s locally, a ratio of 3.6 to 4.0. At 4.0 the five files would read 7.2 / 6.5 / 9.7 / 5.0 / 8.8 s; session-grants and rotated-token are the closest to the line. The card's pin, "the next refresh PR's list no longer names the file", is the measurement that decides.

**Fewer derivations.** The same counting probe at the head: consolidation 130 to 6, admin-impersonate 95 to 7, session-grants 86 to 32, re-enrollment 48 to 8, rotated-token 63 to 18 real production-parameter derivations per file run.

**Same cases, same expectations.** No ablation is owed for a speed-only change; the evidence is the case lists and the `expect` lines.
- Case names and statuses (sorted `fullName` plus status), before run 1 against each of the three after-runs: identical every time (37/37, 24/24, 17/17, 14/14, 33/33 passed).
- Every `expect` line in the six edited test files is byte-identical between base and head (sorted line diff): `expect(` counts before/after: bearer-rotation 34/34, consolidation 34/34, admin-impersonate 35/35, session-grants 36/36, re-enrollment 41/41, rotated-token 69/69. The `it(` and `describe` lines are identical apart from `describe` becoming `describe.concurrent`. No timeout is raised or lowered, nothing is deleted, nothing moves to another project.

**The shared sign-ups are the same start state** (temporary probes, never committed). For each arrangement, the per-case sign-up flow and the clone flow were run side by side and compared after the full arrangement: per-table row counts and column sets, and the caller's session payload from `getSession`.
- consolidation, with three seed shapes (none, platform admin, org owner): identical tables and identical payloads;
- bearer-rotation (admin promoted, signed in): identical, sign-in 200 on both;
- admin-impersonate (grant, two sign-ins): identical, admin payload `positions: [platform_admin, everyone]` on both.
- Isolation: a write on one copy is seen neither by a second copy nor by the template, and no row object is shared.

## Local verification (head `7fcbf26fa4`, merged with `origin/main` at `66949b7729`)

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-auth run typecheck`: exit 0. All seven files are in `tsconfig.test.json`'s program (`tsc --listFilesOnly`: 7 of 7), the testkit also in `tsconfig.json`'s, and `test-typecheck-debt.json` is unchanged (10 files, 94 errors, 23 signatures).
- The whole package, `vitest run --maxWorkers=2` over all 137 test files in five chunks: 137 files passed, 2791 tests passed, 10 skipped (all in `driver-fault-auth-log-carriers.test.ts`, untouched). The dependency closure was rebuilt first.
- ESLint, narrowed to this diff's 7 files (`--no-inline-config --format json`): 7 files linted, 0 errors, 0 warnings. No ignore covers them, so the population is exactly this diff, and `eslint.config.mjs` never enables type-aware linting (no `parserOptions.project`), so these files cannot change a verdict on an untouched file. The full `pnpm lint` runs in CI.
- Gates: `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands` (no paths; change set = these 7 files against the merge base `66949b7729`) derived 53 commands, the same list as the dispatch's reading. All 53 exit 0 at `7fcbf26fa4`, each run separately with its exit code captured before any pipe; `dispatch-gates --ran` reconciliation: 53 derived, 53 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN. The four artifact-roster gates whose rosters sit under these paths (`check:auth-mount-ledger`, `check:authz-resolver`, `check:error-code-casing`, `check:filter-alias-parity`) also exit 0. `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` needs every package built; it ran after a full `turbo run build` (75 of 75 tasks). Not run locally: the rows the derivation lists outside its 53 (path-scheduled Test Core, Build Core and dogfood jobs, the type-check lanes, the artifact-roster families). Those belong to CI.

## Rows not answered here

These share neither cause, or need more than this mechanism; each is left named for the next slice.

- `scim-deactivation-reconcile-user.test.ts` (35.3 s): 11 s of its 18.4 s local wall is two real-time waits for a timed ban to expire (2 x 5.5 s); the rest is twelve per-case sqlite and SCIM boots and ten fresh-salt hashes of one fixture password, nine of which one shared fixture hash could serve. It needs a controlled clock for the two expiry cases and boot sharing.
- `org-create-posture-gate.test.ts` (11.6 s): 25 cases each sign one user up under a per-case `process.env` posture: 25 fresh-salt derivations, zero memo hits, and the environment rules out concurrency. A module-top vendor load measured 4 to 8 percent.
- `implicit-account-linking.test.ts` (11.7 s): 14 fresh-salt derivations, zero memo hits; a per-test global `fetch` stub and a module-level IdP profile rule out concurrency. Module-top vendor load: 5 to 7 percent.
- `dev-admin-seed-credential-gate.test.ts` (10.3 s): every case sets `NODE_ENV` and the seed environment; the memo answers 3 of 12 derivations (13 to 16 percent of the wall). Its vendor load cannot move to module top, because better-auth captures `NODE_ENV` at first load and these cases run under `development`.
- `last-admin-guard.test.ts` (10.9 s): no scrypt at all; 110 cases each boot their own ObjectQL and sqlite engine (2.5 s locally, a CI ratio up to 4.4).

## Acceptance notes

- Each of these files also spends about 18 to 21 s in vitest import and transform on this box, before and after; that time is outside the per-file reading this budget grades. Noted only.
- No `Test Core` reading exists yet for the concurrent shapes; see the caveat under CI projection.

## Changeset

None. The diff is tests only (six `*.test.ts` files and one `src/__tests__/*.testkit.ts`). The package ships `files: [dist, README.md, CHANGELOG.md]`, and its tsup entries (`src/index.ts`, `src/rate-limit-storage.ts`) reach none of these files, so nothing published changes. `skip-changeset` applies.
